newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest maize, wheat slide on export outlook.
newsitem.headline: Budapest maize, wheat slide on export outlook.

text.p: Wheat and maize futures edged mostly lower on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on mounting fears that excess grain stocks will not find an export market, dealers said.
"The slow slide of the last few days continued," said Tamas Kobulniczky of Swap Ugynoki Kft.
Among the most active maturities, May maize closed at 18,400 forints a tonne, down 60, and May milling wheat ended at 27,300, down 250.
Turnover was 379.1 million forints or 805 contracts.
The decision of the Polish government to introduce a 10 percent duty on grain imports will probably close one of the few remaining markets for old crop maize, said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
With most neighbouring countries having record maize crops last year, only the Czech Republic's 25,000 tonnes quota for Hungarian maize remained to be filled from the old crop.
Hungarian maize stocks were estimated at between 500,000 and one million tonnes, Monostori said.
Players were also selling the new crop, particularly maize, on the belief that surplus stocks would depress the market after the summer harvest, he said.
Kobulniczky said the price would have fallen more today had the dollar not risen against the forint.
In the Budapest interbank market, the forint ended at 170.20/30 against yesterday's close of 169.22/27.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts. @
